text:
finn: Heads-up: dashboard shows weird percentiles for /v2/generate — p50 240ms, p95 180ms, p99 910ms for a small client slice.
leila: That inversion usually means mixed measurement points or tiny sample_count. What's the sample_count?
finn: sample_count=22 for that slice. I pulled via: GET /internal/telemetry/latency?endpoint=/v2/generate&quantiles=0.5,0.95,0.99&group_by=client_tag
omar: 22 samples -> noisy. Also check route variants; we started routing a 1% fallback yesterday to disk-cache pool.
leila: Can we tag quantiles with measurement_point and sample_count? UI should show confidence.
finn: Agreed. Right now console only shows pXX scalars. People assume parity across slices.
omar: Ops-bot: ops-bot: adding note: metric_series=ms-80421, last_seen=2026-03-22T12:01:11Z, tags=[route:fallback-disk-cache, measurement_point:model_generate_start].
leila: Two options: (A) keep numbers and add sample_count_pXX + ci_pXX metadata, or (B) hide quantiles when sample_count < threshold. I prefer A + UI hint.
finn: Also we should include route_policy and route_reason in the telemetry row so console can say "routed to fallback (quota)".
omar: Adding route_reason increases tag cardinality; let's restrict to enums from routing-service.
leila: Good call. For alerts: update p95 SLO evaluation to ignore cohorts with sample_count_p95 < 100 to avoid flapping.
finn: I'll open a tiny RFC: extend telemetry response with sample_count_pXX, ci_pXX, measurement_point and route_reason_enum. Console mock to show faint stripe + tooltip for low-sample quantiles.
omar: :thumbsup: deploy-bot: deploying telemetry-api v1.3.2 (canary) in us-east in 5m. Monitor p99 per-host after deploy.
leila: Thanks — if canary still shows tail on fallback we should either warm that pool or reduce fallthrough.
finn: filing follow-up if tail persists.
